paraphrase: Returning to his cave at Red Rock Jewel Valley, Milarepa found demons who would not leave when he tried to drive them away; when he sang that demons are his own mind's projections and that he had no fear of them, they vanished.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Story 1 in the usual (Chang) arrangement.

paraphrase: In many songs Milarepa urges giving up the eight worldly concerns — gain and loss, pleasure and pain, praise and blame, fame and disgrace — and living in solitude.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. A recurrent theme; no locator.

paraphrase: Gampopa reported to Milarepa his meditative experiences — visions of deities and lights, bliss — and Milarepa answered that these were neither good nor bad, and that he should keep practising without attachment.

paraphrase: At Mount Kailash (Tise) Milarepa contested the Bön priest Naro Bönchung in displays of power and won; the tradition tells it as the mountain passing to the Buddhists.

paraphrase: Snowed in for months on Lachi (Drakar Taso region), Milarepa was thought dead; he survived through inner heat and sang of the snow and his practice.

paraphrase: Milarepa's songs set out the view (to look at one's own mind), meditation (to rest without distraction), conduct (to act without attachment) and fruition (to be free of hope and fear).

paraphrase: When Rechungpa, returned from India, grew proud of his learning, Milarepa sheltered from a hailstorm inside a yak horn without the horn growing or himself shrinking, and sang to humble his disciple's pride.
